scenes.text: Mining was never the destination. It is how you prove the megawatts are real.
53 MW of Nigerian flare-gas capacity was announced in 2025 with the sequence stated out loud: Bitcoin first because it deploys fastest, then AI compute and cloud on the same power.
Green Flare said it at announcement: Bitcoin first because it is easiest to deploy and monetise, then AI compute and cloud services on the same flare gas.
TeraWulf proved the back half of that sequence in Q1 2026, when HPC lease revenue passed mining revenue at the company for the first time.
Crusoe walked the whole arc: more than 425 modular data centers deployed on stranded gas, then a sale of the mining business to focus on AI infrastructure.
Calling this a pivot misreads it. Mining is not being abandoned. It is being used as the commissioning load that makes a remote site bankable enough to host anything else.
Same site, same containers, different tenant. That is the whole thesis.

title: Bitcoin Mining Is the On-Ramp. It Was Never the Destination.
